guards.what: N1: `player.block = 10` (sturdy_clamp.py:30) vs `CreatureCmd.LoseBlock(creature, block - 10)` (SturdyClamp.cs:42), and the `block != 0` / `block > 10` structure
guards.rationale: Arithmetically identical -- losing (block - 10) from block leaves exactly 10 -- and the direct assignment cannot skip a side effect here, verified in both directions. C# side: CreatureCmd.LoseBlock (CreatureCmd.cs:666-678) fires Hook.AfterBlockBroken only when `block > 0 && creature.Block <= 0`, and this call is guarded by `block > 10` so the result is always exactly 10 > 0 -- AfterBlockBroken can never fire from the cap. Sim side EXECUTED (b15-clamp): a sentinel with an after_block_broken listener records NOTHING when the cap fires on 30 block. C#'s outer `if (block != 0)` exists only to skip the Flash on a zero-block turn, and the inner `block > 10` matches the port's `if player.block > self.MAX_RETAINED`. The constants agree three ways: `_maxRetainedBlock = 10` (SturdyClamp.cs:14), BlockVar(10m, ValueProp.Unpowered) (SturdyClamp.cs:18) and MAX_RETAINED = 10 (sturdy_clamp.py:21), with no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file.

guards.what: N2: `creature != base.Owner.Creature` on both overrides (SturdyClamp.cs:24, 33) vs `creature is not self.player` / the un-guarded on_player_turn_start
guards.rationale: should_clear_block IS dispatched for enemies in the sim (combat.py's enemy turn-start arm), so sturdy_clamp.py:25's identity test is load-bearing and correct -- it lets every enemy clear normally, exactly as SturdyClamp.cs:24-28 returns true for a non-owner. The cap's own owner test is structurally satisfied because on_player_turn_start is only ever dispatched for the player (player.py:169). Note that C# compares CREATURE IDENTITY here rather than SIDE, and so does the port, so there is no side-vs-identity divergence of the kind relic/unsettling_lamp G3 records.
